### [Adobe’s Firefly Gets a Creative Agent to Orchestrate All of Creative Cloud](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/04/adobe-new-creative-agent)
**What’s new?** Adobe [unveiled Firefly AI Assistant](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/04/adobe-new-creative-agent), a new creative agent that lets designers describe a vision in natural language and orchestrates complex, multi-step workflows across Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, and other Creative Cloud apps from a single conversational interface.
**What matters?**
* The assistant integrates **30+ AI models** — including Kling 3.0, Runway Gen-4.5, Google’s Veo 3.1, and ElevenLabs — giving creators access to the industry’s best video, audio, and image generators from within one Creative Cloud workflow.
* A new integration with [Frame.io](https://blog.adobe.com/en/publish/2026/04/15/the-age-of-creative-agents-rise-creative-director) lets stakeholders leave feedback directly in Frame, with the assistant automatically interpreting those notes and applying changes using the appropriate tools.
* Adobe is also integrating Firefly AI Assistant with Anthropic’s Claude, letting creators **conceptualize a project in Claude** and execute it directly through Firefly without switching platforms.
**Why it matters?**
Adobe’s decision to pull Kling, Runway, ElevenLabs, and Google Veo under one roof signals a move away from closed creative ecosystems — Firefly is becoming less a toolset and more a creative command center. The public beta launches within weeks, and new video and image features are available immediately for Firefly subscribers.

### [Claude Opus 4.7 Triples Vision Resolution and Sharpens Creative Design Output](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-7)
**What’s new?** Anthropic [released Claude Opus 4.7](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-7), an upgrade over Opus 4.6 that triples the model’s image resolution handling and delivers noticeably better output quality for creative work — including UI design, slides, and documents — at unchanged pricing.
**What matters?**
* Vision now processes images up to **2,576 pixels** on the long edge — roughly 3.75 megapixels and more than triple the capacity of earlier Claude versions — enabling accurate analysis of dense screenshots, detailed diagrams, and high-resolution design files.
* Coding benchmarks jumped from 53.4% to 64.3% on SWE-bench Pro, and Opus 4.7 [ranked #1 on the Vals AI Vibe Code Benchmark](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-7) at 71%, making it a strong choice for teams building AI-assisted creative tools.
* Pricing stays at $5/$25 per million tokens, with availability via the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry — though a new tokenizer may increase token consumption by up to **1.35×** depending on content type.
**Why it matters?**
For creative professionals using Claude in design and development workflows, the jump in resolution handling means the model can now meaningfully engage with real-world visual assets instead of low-res thumbnails. Better interface and document output quality puts Opus 4.7 in direct contention as a production tool for AI-assisted design work.

the 'work smart, not hard' trap 👎

Mohamed Ali are tech careers sprinting marathons?  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌
The saying "
**Work smart, not hard**" drives me nuts Mohamed Ali.
In any dog-eat-dog environment (like the current tech job market) almost everyone you're competing against to keep your current job, or get your next job is "working smart".
94% of the time when a career coaching client
https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~jus2zKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL of mine says
****  "I'm trying to work smart, not hard" ****
I dig into their thought process, and we end up realizing it's just a way for their ego to excuse their poor work ethic.
Falling into the "I work smart, not hard" line of reasoning is mentally attractive because when confronted with failure, it's much easier for most of us to think
**    "hey I'm smart but just got unlucky"**
Rather than think confront our inner demons and say:
**  "hey I'm lazy and my problems can directly
be fixed by me putting in more time & effort"**
Now I get it, you might be thinking....
****    "STFU Nick, life is a marathon, NOT a sprint"****
But I've got a reply for that too - meet Eliud.
Eliud Kipchoge is the first person to run a marathon in under 2 hours.
To put that in perspective, he's running a 4:34 mile....
EVERY SINGLE MILE FOR 26 MILES.
For my metric friends, that's a 2:40 per KM pace, and he's doing that for 42km!
So, whenever someone brings up "life is marathon, not a sprint" keep in mind:
**At elite levels, marathon runners are going faster than 99% of people can sprint a mile!**
If you want to be at the top of your field, yes, life is a marathon, BUT you basically gotta be sprinting it too!
This is why, for those who aspire to land top jobs in big-tech it's not enough to say "I work hard, not smart".
You gotta work very hard AND work very smart to get those huuge FAANG paychecks.
Sam Altman, founder & CEO of OpenAI (the company behind chatGPT) comes to a similar conclusion:
**"You can get to about the 90th percentile in your field by working either smart or hard, which is still a great accomplishment.
But getting to the 99th percentile requires both-you will be competing with other very talented people who will have great ideas and be willing to work
a lot"**
For more interesting perspectives on hard work & career success, here's some of my favorite articles:
* Paul Graham - How To Work Hard https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~jus3zKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL
* Auren Hoffman - Why Hard Work is Under-Rated https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~jus4zKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL
* Sam Altman - How To Be Successful https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~juwvzKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL
Till next time,
**Nick Singh**
Founder of SQL Prep Site DataLemur https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~juwwzKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL
Author of Ace the Data Science Interview
https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~jus1zKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL

p.s. If this email motivated to get serious, and you're ready to grind your way to your dream job in data, check out my video course Ace the Data Job Hunt https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~juwxzKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL.

EP211: How the JVM Works

View this post on the web at https://blog.bytebytego.com/p/ep211-how-the-jvm-works
This week’s system design refresher:
AI for Engineering Leaders: Course Direction Survey
What is a Data Lakehouse? (Youtube video)
How the JVM Works
Figma Design to Code, Code to Design: Clearly Explained
12 AI Papers that Changed Everything
How Load Balancers Work?
Optimistic locking vs pessimistic locking
AI for Engineering Leaders: Course Direction Survey
We are working on a course, AI for Engineering Leaders, and would appreciate your help with a quick survey.
Before we build it, we want to get it right, so we’re asking the people who would actually take it. If you’re an EM, Tech Lead, Director, or VP of Engineering, I’d love 3 minutes of your time. This quick survey covers questions like: how do you evaluate engineers when AI writes most of the code? What metrics still matter? Where do AI tools actually help versus just add noise?
Your answers will directly shape what we cover. Thank you!
What is a Data Lakehouse?
How the JVM Works
We compile, run, and debug Java code all the time. But what exactly does the JVM do between compile and run?
Here's the flow:
Build: javac compiles your source code into platform-independent bytecode, stored as .class files, JARs, or modules.
Load: The class loader subsystem brings in classes as needed using parent delegation. Bootstrap handles core JDK classes, Platform covers extensions, and System loads your application code.
Link: The Verify step checks bytecode safety. Prepare allocates static fields with default values, and Resolve turns symbolic references into direct memory addresses.
Initialize: Static variables are assigned their actual values, and static initializer blocks execute. This happens only the first time the class is used.
Memory: Heap and Method Area are shared across threads. The JVM stack, PC register, and native method stack are created per thread. The garbage collector reclaims unused heap memory.
Execute: The interpreter runs bytecode directly. When a method gets called multiple times, the JIT compiler converts it to native machine code and stores it in the code cache. Native calls go through JNI to reach C/C++ libraries.
Run: Your program runs on a mix of interpreted and JIT-compiled code. Fast startup, peak performance over time.
Figma Design to Code, Code to Design: Clearly Explained
We spoke with the Figma team behind these releases to better understand the details and engineering challenges. This article covers how Figma’s design-to-code and code-to-design workflows actually work, starting with why the obvious approaches fail, how MCP solves them, and the engineering challenges that remain.
At the high level:
Design to Code:
Step 1: Once the user provides a Figma link and prompt, the coding agent requests the list of available tools from Figma’s MCP server.
Step 2: The server returns its tools: get_design_context, get_metadata, and more.
Step 3: The agent calls get_design_context with the file key and node ID parsed from the URL.
Step 4: The MCP server returns a structured representation including layout and styles. The agent then generates working code (React, Vue, Swift, etc.) using that structured context.
Code to Design:
Step 1: Once the user provides the desired UI code, the agent discovers available tools from the MCP server.
Step 2: The agent calls generate_figma_design with the current UI code.
Step 3: The MCP tool opens the running UI in a browser and injects a capture script.
Step 4: The user selects the desired component, and the script sends the selected DOM data to the server.
Step 5: The server maps the DOM to native Figma layers: frames, auto-layout groups, and editable text layers. The result is fully editable Figma layers shown to the user.
Read the full newsletter here. [ https://substack.com/redirect/3f589db1-a4f5-4ffd-90c9-706302534970?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ]
12 AI Papers that Changed Everything
A handful of research papers shaped the entire AI landscape we see today.
The diagram below highlights 12 that we consider especially influential.
AlexNet (2012): Showed deep neural nets can see. Ignited the deep learning era
GANs (2014): Generate realistic image by having two networks compete
Transformer (2017): Google's "Attention Is All You Need." The architecture behind everything
GPT-3 (2020): OpenAI showed scale unlocks emergent abilities.
InstructGPT (2022): OpenAI introduced RLHF. Turned raw LLMs into useful assistants.
Scaling Laws (2020): Loss follows a clean power law
ViT (2020): Split images into patches and use a Transformer for vision tasks.
Latent Diffusion (2021): Denoising in compressed space. The design behind DALL·E.
DDPM (2020): Add noise, then learn to reverse it. The foundation behind diffusion models.
CLIP (2021): OpenAI connected images and text in one shared space.
Chain-of-Thought (2022): A simple prompt that unlocked complex reasoning.
RAG (2020): Retrieve real documents, then generate. Grounded LLMs in facts.
Over to you: What paper is missing from this list?
How Load Balancers Work?
A load balancer is a system that distributes incoming traffic across multiple servers to ensure no single server gets overloaded. Here’s how it works under the hood:
The client sends a request to the load balancer.
A listener receives it on the right port/protocol (HTTP/HTTPS, TCP).
The load balancer parses the packet to understand headers and intent.
It checks recent health checks to know which backend servers are up.
It looks in the connection table to reuse any existing client-to-server mapping.
Using its rules, it picks a healthy target server for this request.
It rewrites addresses so traffic can reach that chosen server.
It completes the TCP handshake to open a reliable connection.
If HTTPS is used, it decrypts (or passes through) via SSL/TLS as configured.
The request is forwarded to the selected backend server.
The backend processes it and sends a response back to the load balancer.
The load balancer may tweak headers, then forwards the response to the client.
Over to you: Which other step will you add to the working of a load balancer?
Optimistic locking vs pessimistic locking
Imagine two developers updating the same database row at the same time. One of them will have their update rejected. How should the system handle this?
There are two common approaches.
Optimistic locking assumes conflicts are rare. Both users read the data without acquiring any lock. Each record carries a version number. When a user attempts to write, the database checks: does the version in your update match the current version in the database? If another transaction already incremented the version from 1 to 2, your update still references version 1. The write is rejected.
Pessimistic locking takes the opposite approach. It assumes conflicts are likely, so it blocks them before they happen. The first transaction locks the row, and every other transaction waits until that lock is released. No version checks needed.
If your system is read-heavy with occasional writes, optimistic locking is the best option. When concurrent writes occur frequently and the cost of a conflict is high, pessimistic locking is the safer choice.
Over to you: Have you ever run into a deadlock in production because of a locking strategy? How did you fix it?

(i shouldn't have been so cheap 😆)
but I loved that red rocket.
I share that story because everyone starts from somewhere.
And whether you want a fancy car or not, it doesn't matter.
What matters is the freedom to choose what to work on.
So today, 5 stories of people who chased the entrepreneur dream.
And maybe even bought their dream cars :)
Welcome to Sunday Breakfast!!
The Orange Juice 🍊
[He made enough to buy himself his dream car](https://youtu.be/qeY283nBhIA?si=EDW1w8DqJJNemR24)
Ok, so the story I shared before was inspired by my friend Jack Friks.
His business made $40,000 last year.
He's one of my favorite builders to follow on X.
He shared his story with us a while back, and it's a GREAT one.
[Watch it here](https://youtu.be/qeY283nBhIA?si=EDW1w8DqJJNemR24)
Congrats, jack!!
The Coffee ☕
[2026 is the year of iOS apps](https://youtu.be/yBjcmMhXSDk?si=LEbmwsGmCU44oFXk)
Apps are making a huge comeback.
I'm seeing dozens and dozens of success stories every day.
Everyone can build them, but the question remains:
How do I grow?
Well, there are dozens of ways to do it, but this is one of my favorites
[Check out this breakdown of how to build and grow a mobile app today](https://youtu.be/yBjcmMhXSDk?si=LEbmwsGmCU44oFXk)
The Special 🍽️
[What's It Really Like To Be A Founder?](https://offers.hubspot.com/hustle-founder-confessions?utm_medium=email-media-newsletter&utm_source=starter-story&utm_campaign=owned&utm_term=2026-04-19&utm_content=native-ads)
The majority of the advice you read online about being a founder is B.S.
Why?
Because most of the advice is written by people who aren't actually building right now.
The only way to learn about what it's like to be a founder/builder is to hear it directly from the source. From people in the real, messy, trenches.
Well, that's exactly what you get with [Founder Confessions.](https://offers.hubspot.com/hustle-founder-confessions?utm_medium=email-media-newsletter&utm_source=starter-story&utm_campaign=owned&utm_term=2026-04-19&utm_content=native-ads)
This free resources includes 72 raw responses from real builders answering three simple questions:
– What do you wish you knew earlier?
– What ideas are you thinking about now?
– What unconventional habits make you sharper?
This database will teach you more in a few minutes than hours of reading guru threads online (trust me).
So, if you are ready to learn the hard-fought lessons from some of the best founders in the world...
[Get All The Data Right Here](https://offers.hubspot.com/hustle-founder-confessions?utm_medium=email-media-newsletter&utm_source=starter-story&utm_campaign=owned&utm_term=2026-04-19&utm_content=native-ads)
The Eggs 🍳
[You've never heard of this $1.5M App](https://youtu.be/bq3-qH-CpYQ?si=Tw-ZgXUaif96d_sY)
Every so often I come across these really interesting apps that just surprise me.
This is one of those examples.
This guy built a really simple app that has made over $1.5M, and I can almost guarantee you've never heard of it.
[This is a really cool story. Watch it all right here.](https://youtu.be/bq3-qH-CpYQ?si=Tw-ZgXUaif96d_sY)
The Toast 🥪
[What Makes An App Worth 7-Figures?](https://youtu.be/_HiyjLNe_LA?si=-fDaC9XZ_MuWyTgb)
A few weeks back, I sat down and chatted with an app buyer over on our second channel, Starter Story Build.
This was a really incredible conversation that gave me insights into how to build an app that might someday be worth over a million dollars.
If you're building something and are hoping to one day exit...
This is a must-watch.
[Check out the full conversation here](https://youtu.be/_HiyjLNe_LA?si=-fDaC9XZ_MuWyTgb)
The Pancakes 🥞
[This side project makes $36K Per Year (for now)](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/live-tourney)
A lot of people I know want to launch a side project...but they don't always know where to start.
Well, this is a great example of a guy who built an app and a hobby that he loved.
And when he submitted this case study, this little side project is making him $36K/year.
But I happen to know that this app has grown a lot since this was published.
So, if you want to learn about the early days of a very successful business, [check this out right here.](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/live-tourney)
That's it!
I hope you have the BEST long weekend and have a great week!
Pat

Color Psychology for Your Personal & Professional Brand

View this post on the web at https://greatcareersphl.substack.com/p/color-psychology
Check out the list of upcoming events in April at Great Careers Network & affiliates for job seekers, entrepreneurs, & employed professionals at the bottom of this article or visit the website.
👉 greatcareers.org/events [ https://substack.com/redirect/b77ae7ed-e0b3-40c2-b416-223e56af4b7f?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ] 👈
Why the Colors You Choose May Shape First Impressions Before You Say a Word
Color speaks before words. People notice your visual identity before your content (bio, resume, website copy, or business pitch, etc.). The colors you choose subtly signal trust, confidence, creativity, calmness, authority, warmth, or energy.
For career professionals and business owners, color isn’t just decoration; it’s a strategy.
Whether you are building a personal brand, refreshing a business identity, launching a side hustle, or reintroducing yourself during a career pivot, thoughtful use of color can help shape perception.
Why Color Matters
Research and branding experts have long explored how color influences mood and decision-making. While reactions vary by culture, age, industry, and personal experience, colors often carry common associations.
Examples:
Blue - Trust, credibility, intelligence, calm
Green - Growth, wellness, money, sustainability
Red - Energy, urgency, boldness, confidence
Orange - Optimism, friendliness, enthusiasm
Yellow - Creativity, optimism, visibility
Purple - Wisdom, imagination, premium feel
Black - Sophistication, authority, power
White - Simplicity, clarity, clean design
Gray - Balance, professionalism, neutrality
The key point: color can influence how people feel about your brand before they consciously analyze it.
Your Personal Brand Has Colors - Even If You Never Chose Them
Many professionals think they “don’t have a brand.” But if you have a website, profile photo, wardrobe, presentation slides, business cards, office décor, or social graphics, you already have one.
Ask yourself:
What colors do I wear professionally?
Which colors dominate my website or marketing materials?
Do my visuals feel aligned or random?
Do people experience consistency across platforms?
Do my colors reflect where I am now or who I used to be?
That last question matters.
Many people keep colors from an old chapter of life. But careers evolve, businesses pivot, and new audiences emerge. Your visual identity should mature with you. We get it! The nonprofit just did a rebrand [ https://substack.com/redirect/c048abd9-56db-4c38-8028-9484742d5bef?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ] at the beginning of 2026!
Choosing Colors Based on Strategy, Not Just Preference
Your favorite color may still belong in your brand. But it should not be the only reason it is there.
Instead, consider:
1. What Do You Want to Be Known For?
If you want to project:
Stability - Blue / Gray
Innovation - Purple / Electric Blue
Warmth - Orange / Gold
Wellness - Green / Earth tones
Executive presence - Navy / Black / White
Creativity - Bold mixed palettes
2. Who Is Your Audience?
A startup founder targeting Gen Z may choose differently from an executive coach targeting Fortune 500 leaders.
3. What Industry Are You In?
Examples:
Finance - Blue, green, navy
Healthcare - Blue, white, green
Tech - Blue, black, modern neutrals
Wellness - Green, earth tones
Creative fields - Brighter, expressive palettes
4. Are You Reinventing Yourself?
A career pivot may deserve a visual reset.
A new chapter may call for new colors.
Where Career Professionals Can Use Color Intentionally
You do not need a major rebrand to benefit from this.
Use color strategically in:
Professional headshots (clothing choices)
Website design
Speaking slides
Resume accent colors (carefully)
Email signatures
Business cards
Social media graphics
Event banners
Office background for video calls
Takeaway: Consistent color choices across all media enhance brand recognition.
Common Mistakes
Avoid these branding traps:
Choosing colors randomly
Using too many competing colors
Following trends without a strategy
Selecting colors that clash with your audience
Ignoring readability and accessibility
Copying another brand too closely
Practical Exercise: Your Color Audit
Take 10 minutes and review your digital presence. Read details about colors on Color Psychology [ https://substack.com/redirect/da605f4d-9820-43d5-8888-2bd56515bbfa?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ]. Have fun checking out the Brand Colors [ https://substack.com/redirect/ee70c76f-2a7f-4329-8f9a-0eb0dd642608?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ] website.
Ask:
What are my top three recurring colors?
What emotions do they create?
Are they helping or hurting credibility?
Do they match my next chapter?
What one small change could improve consistency?
Final Thought
Your brand is not only what you say. It is also what people sense.
Color quickly creates emotional cues, visual memory, and a sense of alignment. To use color effectively: Use it intentionally to reinforce your message, and avoid careless choices that can dilute it.
You do not need a Fortune 500 budget to think like a brand strategist.
Sometimes a career reinvention starts with a better sentence.
Sometimes it starts with a better color palette.
You may or may not have heard of Pantone Colors [ https://substack.com/redirect/22885d03-6f7b-46aa-9ac6-f1f7b6e5f38b?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ] or HTML Color Codes, Hex Color Codes, RGB, and HSL Values [ https://substack.com/redirect/b348adf9-96fc-4d05-b5f4-6ee114b1dac6?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ], so check out these sites to learn more.
Canva [ https://substack.com/redirect/51006654-63a3-439e-8e90-851aca2bc065?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ], which I use daily, has color palette generators, ideas, and more, so you can set up your brand kit for consistency. Join an upcoming Snazzy Graphics workshop (noted below)!
Call to Action
If you are rethinking your professional identity, career pivot, business presence, or personal brand, upcoming workshops (see details below) and/or strategic coaching can help you align the message and the visuals.
Your next chapter may deserve more than an update. It may deserve a full repositioning. Book a 1:1 discovery call [ https://substack.com/redirect/15459cf6-b5eb-4e60-9bfa-c978af0f41d6?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ] if you have questions, or need information or resources.

# 🇬🇧[** UK launches £500 million Sovereign AI fund to back homegrown founders**](https://www.sovereignai.gov.uk/)
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cf31b3fa-b28c-4601-8afa-afd373b7c86d/image.png?t=1776267741)
Follow image link: (https://www.sovereignai.gov.uk/)
Caption:
**The Inside:** The UK is launching [Sovereign AI today](https://www.sovereignai.gov.uk/), a new £500M venture fund designed to help British AI founders start, scale, and compete globally. The fund will be chaired by Balderton partner James Wise and gives startups more than just capital. Portfolio companies will also get access to large scale compute, government datasets, and faster procurement pathways into the public sector.
**The details:**
* Sovereign AI is launching on April 16 with £500M to support UK AI founders from day one
* The fund will combine capital with access to major AI compute infrastructure and proprietary datasets
* It also plans to give startups faster procurement routes, potentially helping them sell into the public sector earlier
* James Wise will chair the initiative, giving the vehicle a clear investor operator profile
* The broader goal is to help founders start, scale, and compete globally from within the UK ecosystem
**Why it matters:** More interesting than the £500M itself is the role the government is taking on. UK venture is already clustering hard around AI, with [74% of all VC funding](https://www.disruptionbanking.com/2026/04/15/uk-vc-investment-gathers-pace-in-q1-2026-as-ai-and-megarounds-drive-late-stage-surge/) going into the sector in Q1. Now the state is stepping into that same market alongside private investors, with a direct hand in how more companies get funded, built, and kept in the UK.
--------------------
--------------------
###### VENTURE CAPITAL
# [⏳ Q1 2026 was the biggest quarter in venture history](https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2044186478163431848)
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9f93fcb3-ae09-4bc6-99e0-aa1196f9fe94/image.png?t=1776261915)
Follow image link: (https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2044186478163431848)
Caption:
**The Inside:** Global [startup funding hit $300B in Q1 2026](https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2044186478163431848), up 153% quarter over quarter and 151% year over year, making it the largest quarter ever recorded. But the headline number is heavily distorted by a small group of mega rounds. AI alone accounted for $242B, or about 80% of all venture funding in the quarter, while just four US companies took in $188B, equal to 65% of the global total.
**The details:**
* Global venture dollar volume reached $300B in Q1 2026, already around 70% of all venture capital invested in full ye
ar 2025
* AI companies raised $242B in Q1 alone, above the roughly $215B AI startups raised across all of 2025
* Late stage funding jumped 281% quarter over quarter to a record $243B, driving most of the surge
* OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Waymo raised a combined $188B, absorbing nearly two thirds of all global venture dollars
* Strip out those four rounds and the quarter looks far less exceptional, especially outside late stage AI infrastructure
**Why it matters:** Strip out four mega rounds and this starts to look like a fairly normal quarter, maybe even a soft one, for venture. The real story is not that VC broadly rebounded. It is that AI infrastructure funding is starting to behave like a separate asset class with its own pricing, scale, and capital requirements. For LPs and GPs, the practical question is whether they have any exposure to that market, or whether they are operating in the other $58B that looks nothing like the headline.

###### AI DATA
# 📊[ Stanford’s AI Index shows 53% adoption, but trust is still stuck at 31%](https://hai.stanford.edu/assets/files/ai_index_report_2026.pdf)
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/29dbb3a4-b08c-4853-bb01-855ca93b0db8/image.png?t=1776263252)
Follow image link: (https://hai.stanford.edu/assets/files/ai_index_report_2026.pdf)
Caption:
**The Inside:** Stanford HAI’s [2026 AI Index](https://hai.stanford.edu/assets/files/ai_index_report_2026.pdf) shows AI has now reached more than half the world’s population, scaling faster than the PC or the internet did at a similar stage. But public trust is moving in the opposite direction. Adoption is rising fast, while confidence in how the technology will affect jobs, institutions, and daily life remains low.
**The details:**
* AI adoption reached 53%, meaning the technology has already spread to more than half the global population
* Almost three quarters of AI experts are optimistic about AI’s impact on jobs, but only 23% of the public agrees
* The US remains the leading builder of AI systems, but ranks just 24th in actual usage at 28.3% adoption
* China has narrowed the model performance gap with the US to 2.7%, while AI researcher migration into the US fell 89%
* Developer employment for workers aged 22 to 25 is down nearly 20% since 2024, even as older engineering cohorts kept growing
**Why it matters:** The gap between adoption and trust is starting to look like one of the most important numbers in AI. The technology is spreading quickly, but the public is much less convinced than the people building it. That matters because AI adoption can keep rising even while political resistance, labor anxiety, and regulatory pressure build underneath it.

###### STORY
# 🏪[** An AI agent got a $100K budget and hired humans to run a store**](https://andonlabs.com/blog/andon-market-launch)
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/953b1987-595f-40ea-a2ad-8263a2c338d2/image.png?t=1776276664)
Follow image link: (https://andonlabs.com/blog/andon-market-launch)
Caption: _Image source: Andon Labs_
**The Inside:** Andon Labs [dropped an AI agent](https://andonlabs.com/blog/andon-market-launch) named Luna into a real retail space with a $100K budget, a credit card, and one goal: turn a profit. Luna came up with the boutique concept, hired workers, and managed the shop, in what may be one of the first real examples of an AI acting like an employer in the physical world.
**The details:**
* Andon Labs’ last experiment was an AI vending machine at Anthropic, while this one gave Luna a three year lease, a $100K budget, and broad autonomy
* Luna’s only directive was to make money, with the agent creating the store concept, posting job listings, and handling interviews over Zoom with the camera off
* The system ran on Claude Sonnet 4.6 for reasoning and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Preview for voice, while observing the store through screenshots from security cameras
* Luna still made obvious mistakes, including selecting Afghanistan in a TaskRabbit dropdown while hiring a painter and messing up the opening weekend staff schedule
**Why it matters:** Real world agent experiments keep showing the same thing: these systems can already handle parts of the job, but they still break in dumb and very human visible ways. The gap is still real, but it is also narrowing. A version of Luna that makes fewer of these mistakes is probably not far off.
--------------------
--------------------
###### FUNDRAISING
# **Everything else in fundraising today**
**Eka** closed a[ $107M second fund ](https://tech.eu/2026/04/13/eka-closes-107m-fund-ii-to-becomes-the-uk-s-largest-early-stage-impact-vc/)to back up to 30 UK pre seed and seed startups across health, sustainability, and essential services, becoming the country’s largest early stage impact VC by fund size.
**Bluefish **raised [$43M in a Series B](https://www.bluefishai.com/blog/bluefish-raises-43-million-series-b-to-power-agentic-marketing-for-the-fortune-500) co led by NEA and Threshold to expand its AI search and brand visibility platform across Fortune 500 marketers.

the 'work smart, not hard' trap 👎

Mohamed Ali are tech careers sprinting marathons?  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌
The saying "
**Work smart, not hard**" drives me nuts Mohamed Ali.
In any dog-eat-dog environment (like the current tech job market) almost everyone you're competing against to keep your current job, or get your next job is "working smart".
94% of the time when a career coaching client
https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~jus2zKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL of mine says
****  "I'm trying to work smart, not hard" ****
I dig into their thought process, and we end up realizing it's just a way for their ego to excuse their poor work ethic.
Falling into the "I work smart, not hard" line of reasoning is mentally attractive because when confronted with failure, it's much easier for most of us to think
**    "hey I'm smart but just got unlucky"**
Rather than think confront our inner demons and say:
**  "hey I'm lazy and my problems can directly
be fixed by me putting in more time & effort"**
Now I get it, you might be thinking....
****    "STFU Nick, life is a marathon, NOT a sprint"****
But I've got a reply for that too - meet Eliud.
Eliud Kipchoge is the first person to run a marathon in under 2 hours.
To put that in perspective, he's running a 4:34 mile....
EVERY SINGLE MILE FOR 26 MILES.
For my metric friends, that's a 2:40 per KM pace, and he's doing that for 42km!
So, whenever someone brings up "life is marathon, not a sprint" keep in mind:
**At elite levels, marathon runners are going faster than 99% of people can sprint a mile!**
If you want to be at the top of your field, yes, life is a marathon, BUT you basically gotta be sprinting it too!
This is why, for those who aspire to land top jobs in big-tech it's not enough to say "I work hard, not smart".
You gotta work very hard AND work very smart to get those huuge FAANG paychecks.
Sam Altman, founder & CEO of OpenAI (the company behind chatGPT) comes to a similar conclusion:
**"You can get to about the 90th percentile in your field by working either smart or hard, which is still a great accomplishment.
But getting to the 99th percentile requires both-you will be competing with other very talented people who will have great ideas and be willing to work
a lot"**

* Auren Hoffman - Why Hard Work is Under-Rated https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~jus4zKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL
* Sam Altman - How To Be Successful https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~juwvzKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL

EP211: How the JVM Works

View this post on the web at https://blog.bytebytego.com/p/ep211-how-the-jvm-works
This week’s system design refresher:
AI for Engineering Leaders: Course Direction Survey
What is a Data Lakehouse? (Youtube video)
How the JVM Works
Figma Design to Code, Code to Design: Clearly Explained
12 AI Papers that Changed Everything
How Load Balancers Work?
Optimistic locking vs pessimistic locking
AI for Engineering Leaders: Course Direction Survey
We are working on a course, AI for Engineering Leaders, and would appreciate your help with a quick survey.
Before we build it, we want to get it right, so we’re asking the people who would actually take it. If you’re an EM, Tech Lead, Director, or VP of Engineering, I’d love 3 minutes of your time. This quick survey covers questions like: how do you evaluate engineers when AI writes most of the code? What metrics still matter? Where do AI tools actually help versus just add noise?
Your answers will directly shape what we cover. Thank you!
What is a Data Lakehouse?
How the JVM Works
We compile, run, and debug Java code all the time. But what exactly does the JVM do between compile and run?
Here's the flow:
Build: javac compiles your source code into platform-independent bytecode, stored as .class files, JARs, or modules.
Load: The class loader subsystem brings in classes as needed using parent delegation. Bootstrap handles core JDK classes, Platform covers extensions, and System loads your application code.
Link: The Verify step checks bytecode safety. Prepare allocates static fields with default values, and Resolve turns symbolic references into direct memory addresses.
Initialize: Static variables are assigned their actual values, and static initializer blocks execute. This happens only the first time the class is used.
Memory: Heap and Method Area are shared across threads. The JVM stack, PC register, and native method stack are created per thread. The garbage collector reclaims unused heap memory.
Execute: The interpreter runs bytecode directly. When a method gets called multiple times, the JIT compiler converts it to native machine code and stores it in the code cache. Native calls go through JNI to reach C/C++ libraries.
Run: Your program runs on a mix of interpreted and JIT-compiled code. Fast startup, peak performance over time.
Figma Design to Code, Code to Design: Clearly Explained
We spoke with the Figma team behind these releases to better understand the details and engineering challenges. This article covers how Figma’s design-to-code and code-to-design workflows actually work, starting with why the obvious approaches fail, how MCP solves them, and the engineering challenges that remain.
At the high level:
Design to Code:
Step 1: Once the user provides a Figma link and prompt, the coding agent requests the list of available tools from Figma’s MCP server.
Step 2: The server returns its tools: get_design_context, get_metadata, and more.
Step 3: The agent calls get_design_context with the file key and node ID parsed from the URL.
Step 4: The MCP server returns a structured representation including layout and styles. The agent then generates working code (React, Vue, Swift, etc.) using that structured context.
Code to Design:
Step 1: Once the user provides the desired UI code, the agent discovers available tools from the MCP server.
Step 2: The agent calls generate_figma_design with the current UI code.
Step 3: The MCP tool opens the running UI in a browser and injects a capture script.
Step 4: The user selects the desired component, and the script sends the selected DOM data to the server.
Step 5: The server maps the DOM to native Figma layers: frames, auto-layout groups, and editable text layers. The result is fully editable Figma layers shown to the user.
Read the full newsletter here. [ https://substack.com/redirect/3f589db1-a4f5-4ffd-90c9-706302534970?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ]
12 AI Papers that Changed Everything
A handful of research papers shaped the entire AI landscape we see today.
The diagram below highlights 12 that we consider especially influential.
AlexNet (2012): Showed deep neural nets can see. Ignited the deep learning era
GANs (2014): Generate realistic image by having two networks compete
Transformer (2017): Google's "Attention Is All You Need." The architecture behind everything
GPT-3 (2020): OpenAI showed scale unlocks emergent abilities.
InstructGPT (2022): OpenAI introduced RLHF. Turned raw LLMs into useful assistants.
Scaling Laws (2020): Loss follows a clean power law
ViT (2020): Split images into patches and use a Transformer for vision tasks.
Latent Diffusion (2021): Denoising in compressed space. The design behind DALL·E.
DDPM (2020): Add noise, then learn to reverse it. The foundation behind diffusion models.
CLIP (2021): OpenAI connected images and text in one shared space.
Chain-of-Thought (2022): A simple prompt that unlocked complex reasoning.
RAG (2020): Retrieve real documents, then generate. Grounded LLMs in facts.
Over to you: What paper is missing from this list?
How Load Balancers Work?
A load balancer is a system that distributes incoming traffic across multiple servers to ensure no single server gets overloaded. Here’s how it works under the hood:
The client sends a request to the load balancer.
A listener receives it on the right port/protocol (HTTP/HTTPS, TCP).
The load balancer parses the packet to understand headers and intent.
It checks recent health checks to know which backend servers are up.
It looks in the connection table to reuse any existing client-to-server mapping.
Using its rules, it picks a healthy target server for this request.
It rewrites addresses so traffic can reach that chosen server.
It completes the TCP handshake to open a reliable connection.
If HTTPS is used, it decrypts (or passes through) via SSL/TLS as configured.
The request is forwarded to the selected backend server.
The backend processes it and sends a response back to the load balancer.
The load balancer may tweak headers, then forwards the response to the client.
Over to you: Which other step will you add to the working of a load balancer?
Optimistic locking vs pessimistic locking
Imagine two developers updating the same database row at the same time. One of them will have their update rejected. How should the system handle this?
There are two common approaches.
Optimistic locking assumes conflicts are rare. Both users read the data without acquiring any lock. Each record carries a version number. When a user attempts to write, the database checks: does the version in your update match the current version in the database? If another transaction already incremented the version from 1 to 2, your update still references version 1. The write is rejected.
Pessimistic locking takes the opposite approach. It assumes conflicts are likely, so it blocks them before they happen. The first transaction locks the row, and every other transaction waits until that lock is released. No version checks needed.
If your system is read-heavy with occasional writes, optimistic locking is the best option. When concurrent writes occur frequently and the cost of a conflict is high, pessimistic locking is the safer choice.
Over to you: Have you ever run into a deadlock in production because of a locking strategy? How did you fix it?

That time I bought my dream car

https://www.starterstory.com/join
Hey!
Let me tell you a quick funny story:
When you start making money online, it's so easy to be tempted to buy all this stuff you don't really need.
Fancy watches, clothes, and gear.
But me?
I bought myself a used Toyota for $3,000 all cash!
The DREAM car!!
Now to be honest... it broke down like 1,000 times over the course of two years.
(i shouldn't have been so cheap 😆)
but I loved that red rocket.
I share that story because everyone starts from somewhere.
And whether you want a fancy car or not, it doesn't matter.
What matters is the freedom to choose what to work on.
So today, 5 stories of people who chased the entrepreneur dream.
And maybe even bought their dream cars :)
Welcome to Sunday Breakfast!!
The Orange Juice 🍊
[He made enough to buy himself his dream car](https://youtu.be/qeY283nBhIA?si=EDW1w8DqJJNemR24)
Ok, so the story I shared before was inspired by my friend Jack Friks.
His business made $40,000 last year.
He's one of my favorite builders to follow on X.
He shared his story with us a while back, and it's a GREAT one.
[Watch it here](https://youtu.be/qeY283nBhIA?si=EDW1w8DqJJNemR24)
Congrats, jack!!
The Coffee ☕
[2026 is the year of iOS apps](https://youtu.be/yBjcmMhXSDk?si=LEbmwsGmCU44oFXk)
Apps are making a huge comeback.
I'm seeing dozens and dozens of success stories every day.
Everyone can build them, but the question remains:
How do I grow?
Well, there are dozens of ways to do it, but this is one of my favorites
[Check out this breakdown of how to build and grow a mobile app today](https://youtu.be/yBjcmMhXSDk?si=LEbmwsGmCU44oFXk)
The Special 🍽️
[What's It Really Like To Be A Founder?](https://offers.hubspot.com/hustle-founder-confessions?utm_medium=email-media-newsletter&utm_source=starter-story&utm_campaign=owned&utm_term=2026-04-19&utm_content=native-ads)
The majority of the advice you read online about being a founder is B.S.
Why?
Because most of the advice is written by people who aren't actually building right now.
The only way to learn about what it's like to be a founder/builder is to hear it directly from the source. From people in the real, messy, trenches.
Well, that's exactly what you get with [Founder Confessions.](https://offers.hubspot.com/hustle-founder-confessions?utm_medium=email-media-newsletter&utm_source=starter-story&utm_campaign=owned&utm_term=2026-04-19&utm_content=native-ads)
This free resources includes 72 raw responses from real builders answering three simple questions:
– What do you wish you knew earlier?
– What ideas are you thinking about now?
– What unconventional habits make you sharper?
This database will teach you more in a few minutes than hours of reading guru threads online (trust me).
So, if you are ready to learn the hard-fought lessons from some of the best founders in the world...
[Get All The Data Right Here](https://offers.hubspot.com/hustle-founder-confessions?utm_medium=email-media-newsletter&utm_source=starter-story&utm_campaign=owned&utm_term=2026-04-19&utm_content=native-ads)
The Eggs 🍳
[You've never heard of this $1.5M App](https://youtu.be/bq3-qH-CpYQ?si=Tw-ZgXUaif96d_sY)
Every so often I come across these really interesting apps that just surprise me.
This is one of those examples.
This guy built a really simple app that has made over $1.5M, and I can almost guarantee you've never heard of it.
[This is a really cool story. Watch it all right here.](https://youtu.be/bq3-qH-CpYQ?si=Tw-ZgXUaif96d_sY)
The Toast 🥪
[What Makes An App Worth 7-Figures?](https://youtu.be/_HiyjLNe_LA?si=-fDaC9XZ_MuWyTgb)
A few weeks back, I sat down and chatted with an app buyer over on our second channel, Starter Story Build.
This was a really incredible conversation that gave me insights into how to build an app that might someday be worth over a million dollars.
If you're building something and are hoping to one day exit...
This is a must-watch.
[Check out the full conversation here](https://youtu.be/_HiyjLNe_LA?si=-fDaC9XZ_MuWyTgb)
The Pancakes 🥞
[This side project makes $36K Per Year (for now)](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/live-tourney)
A lot of people I know want to launch a side project...but they don't always know where to start.
Well, this is a great example of a guy who built an app and a hobby that he loved.
And when he submitted this case study, this little side project is making him $36K/year.
But I happen to know that this app has grown a lot since this was published.
So, if you want to learn about the early days of a very successful business, [check this out right here.](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/live-tourney)
That's it!
I hope you have the BEST long weekend and have a great week!
Pat

4e1a08c4-56e2-4ce6-a0a6-a211066e5a03.source_text:
the 'work smart, not hard' trap 👎

Mohamed Ali are tech careers sprinting marathons?  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌
The saying "
**Work smart, not hard**" drives me nuts Mohamed Ali.
In any dog-eat-dog environment (like the current tech job market) almost everyone you're competing against to keep your current job, or get your next job is "working smart".
94% of the time when a career coaching client
https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~jus2zKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL of mine says
****  "I'm trying to work smart, not hard" ****
I dig into their thought process, and we end up realizing it's just a way for their ego to excuse their poor work ethic.
Falling into the "I work smart, not hard" line of reasoning is mentally attractive because when confronted with failure, it's much easier for most of us to think
**    "hey I'm smart but just got unlucky"**
Rather than think confront our inner demons and say:
**  "hey I'm lazy and my problems can directly
be fixed by me putting in more time & effort"**
Now I get it, you might be thinking....
****    "STFU Nick, life is a marathon, NOT a sprint"****
But I've got a reply for that too - meet Eliud.
Eliud Kipchoge is the first person to run a marathon in under 2 hours.
To put that in perspective, he's running a 4:34 mile....
EVERY SINGLE MILE FOR 26 MILES.
For my metric friends, that's a 2:40 per KM pace, and he's doing that for 42km!
So, whenever someone brings up "life is marathon, not a sprint" keep in mind:
**At elite levels, marathon runners are going faster than 99% of people can sprint a mile!**
If you want to be at the top of your field, yes, life is a marathon, BUT you basically gotta be sprinting it too!
This is why, for those who aspire to land top jobs in big-tech it's not enough to say "I work hard, not smart".
You gotta work very hard AND work very smart to get those huuge FAANG paychecks.
Sam Altman, founder & CEO of OpenAI (the company behind chatGPT) comes to a similar conclusion:
**"You can get to about the 90th percentile in your field by working either smart or hard, which is still a great accomplishment.
But getting to the 99th percentile requires both-you will be competing with other very talented people who will have great ideas and be willing to work
a lot"**
For more interesting perspectives on hard work & career success, here's some of my favorite articles:
* Paul Graham - How To Work Hard https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~jus3zKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL
* Auren Hoffman - Why Hard Work is Under-Rated https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~jus4zKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL
* Sam Altman - How To Be Successful https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~juwvzKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL
Till next time,
**Nick Singh**
Founder of SQL Prep Site DataLemur https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~juwwzKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL
Author of Ace the Data Science Interview
https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~jus1zKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL

p.s. If this email motivated to get serious, and you're ready to grind your way to your dream job in data, check out my video course Ace the Data Job Hunt https://nicksingh79965.acemlna.com/lt.php?x=41Zy~GDIVqWZEH_~zg-4gOBu2qBUkQMik~pijHTHIXXL7pWqzky.yuFw5X2nmNE~juwxzKV7I3mg6pR5NA6IiRTi2HEkjNP0jDZ1zHL.

Very few of the tips in
the course are "easy hacks" - most of the advice in there takes effort to execute successfully.
But when you put in the work, like the folks below, great things are destined to happen.

Color Psychology for Your Personal & Professional Brand

View this post on the web at https://greatcareersphl.substack.com/p/color-psychology
Check out the list of upcoming events in April at Great Careers Network & affiliates for job seekers, entrepreneurs, & employed professionals at the bottom of this article or visit the website.
👉 greatcareers.org/events [ https://substack.com/redirect/b77ae7ed-e0b3-40c2-b416-223e56af4b7f?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ] 👈
Why the Colors You Choose May Shape First Impressions Before You Say a Word
Color speaks before words. People notice your visual identity before your content (bio, resume, website copy, or business pitch, etc.). The colors you choose subtly signal trust, confidence, creativity, calmness, authority, warmth, or energy.
For career professionals and business owners, color isn’t just decoration; it’s a strategy.
Whether you are building a personal brand, refreshing a business identity, launching a side hustle, or reintroducing yourself during a career pivot, thoughtful use of color can help shape perception.
Why Color Matters
Research and branding experts have long explored how color influences mood and decision-making. While reactions vary by culture, age, industry, and personal experience, colors often carry common associations.
Examples:
Blue - Trust, credibility, intelligence, calm
Green - Growth, wellness, money, sustainability
Red - Energy, urgency, boldness, confidence
Orange - Optimism, friendliness, enthusiasm
Yellow - Creativity, optimism, visibility
Purple - Wisdom, imagination, premium feel
Black - Sophistication, authority, power
White - Simplicity, clarity, clean design
Gray - Balance, professionalism, neutrality
The key point: color can influence how people feel about your brand before they consciously analyze it.
Your Personal Brand Has Colors - Even If You Never Chose Them
Many professionals think they “don’t have a brand.” But if you have a website, profile photo, wardrobe, presentation slides, business cards, office décor, or social graphics, you already have one.
Ask yourself:
What colors do I wear professionally?
Which colors dominate my website or marketing materials?
Do my visuals feel aligned or random?
Do people experience consistency across platforms?
Do my colors reflect where I am now or who I used to be?
That last question matters.
Many people keep colors from an old chapter of life. But careers evolve, businesses pivot, and new audiences emerge. Your visual identity should mature with you. We get it! The nonprofit just did a rebrand [ https://substack.com/redirect/c048abd9-56db-4c38-8028-9484742d5bef?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ] at the beginning of 2026!
Choosing Colors Based on Strategy, Not Just Preference
Your favorite color may still belong in your brand. But it should not be the only reason it is there.
Instead, consider:
1. What Do You Want to Be Known For?
If you want to project:
Stability - Blue / Gray
Innovation - Purple / Electric Blue
Warmth - Orange / Gold
Wellness - Green / Earth tones
Executive presence - Navy / Black / White
Creativity - Bold mixed palettes
2. Who Is Your Audience?
A startup founder targeting Gen Z may choose differently from an executive coach targeting Fortune 500 leaders.
3. What Industry Are You In?
Examples:
Finance - Blue, green, navy
Healthcare - Blue, white, green
Tech - Blue, black, modern neutrals
Wellness - Green, earth tones
Creative fields - Brighter, expressive palettes
4. Are You Reinventing Yourself?
A career pivot may deserve a visual reset.
A new chapter may call for new colors.
Where Career Professionals Can Use Color Intentionally
You do not need a major rebrand to benefit from this.
Use color strategically in:
Professional headshots (clothing choices)
Website design
Speaking slides
Resume accent colors (carefully)
Email signatures
Business cards
Social media graphics
Event banners
Office background for video calls
Takeaway: Consistent color choices across all media enhance brand recognition.
Common Mistakes
Avoid these branding traps:
Choosing colors randomly
Using too many competing colors
Following trends without a strategy
Selecting colors that clash with your audience
Ignoring readability and accessibility
Copying another brand too closely
Practical Exercise: Your Color Audit
Take 10 minutes and review your digital presence. Read details about colors on Color Psychology [ https://substack.com/redirect/da605f4d-9820-43d5-8888-2bd56515bbfa?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ]. Have fun checking out the Brand Colors [ https://substack.com/redirect/ee70c76f-2a7f-4329-8f9a-0eb0dd642608?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ] website.
Ask:
What are my top three recurring colors?
What emotions do they create?
Are they helping or hurting credibility?
Do they match my next chapter?
What one small change could improve consistency?
Final Thought
Your brand is not only what you say. It is also what people sense.
Color quickly creates emotional cues, visual memory, and a sense of alignment. To use color effectively: Use it intentionally to reinforce your message, and avoid careless choices that can dilute it.
You do not need a Fortune 500 budget to think like a brand strategist.
Sometimes a career reinvention starts with a better sentence.
Sometimes it starts with a better color palette.
You may or may not have heard of Pantone Colors [ https://substack.com/redirect/22885d03-6f7b-46aa-9ac6-f1f7b6e5f38b?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ] or HTML Color Codes, Hex Color Codes, RGB, and HSL Values [ https://substack.com/redirect/b348adf9-96fc-4d05-b5f4-6ee114b1dac6?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ], so check out these sites to learn more.
Canva [ https://substack.com/redirect/51006654-63a3-439e-8e90-851aca2bc065?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ], which I use daily, has color palette generators, ideas, and more, so you can set up your brand kit for consistency. Join an upcoming Snazzy Graphics workshop (noted below)!
Call to Action
If you are rethinking your professional identity, career pivot, business presence, or personal brand, upcoming workshops (see details below) and/or strategic coaching can help you align the message and the visuals.
Your next chapter may deserve more than an update. It may deserve a full repositioning. Book a 1:1 discovery call [ https://substack.com/redirect/15459cf6-b5eb-4e60-9bfa-c978af0f41d6?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ] if you have questions, or need information or resources.

Aside from writing keyword-focused content for ATS resumes and LinkedIn profiles, Lynne is a contributing author on “Applying to Positions” in Find Your Fit: A Practical Guide to Landing the Job You Love [ https://substack.com/redirect/2d0d9dfb-c81a-434c-b309-3266520a3b5e?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ], along with the late Dick Bolles, the author of What Color is Your Parachute?, and is also a speaker and writer on career topics [ https://substack.com/redirect/7464847e-0324-4f5c-a941-11ed030e1556?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ].

###### BREAKING
# 🇬🇧[** UK launches £500 million Sovereign AI fund to back homegrown founders**](https://www.sovereignai.gov.uk/)
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cf31b3fa-b28c-4601-8afa-afd373b7c86d/image.png?t=1776267741)
Follow image link: (https://www.sovereignai.gov.uk/)
Caption:
**The Inside:** The UK is launching [Sovereign AI today](https://www.sovereignai.gov.uk/), a new £500M venture fund designed to help British AI founders start, scale, and compete globally. The fund will be chaired by Balderton partner James Wise and gives startups more than just capital. Portfolio companies will also get access to large scale compute, government datasets, and faster procurement pathways into the public sector.
**The details:**
* Sovereign AI is launching on April 16 with £500M to support UK AI founders from day one
* The fund will combine capital with access to major AI compute infrastructure and proprietary datasets
* It also plans to give startups faster procurement routes, potentially helping them sell into the public sector earlier
* James Wise will chair the initiative, giving the vehicle a clear investor operator profile
* The broader goal is to help founders start, scale, and compete globally from within the UK ecosystem
**Why it matters:** More interesting than the £500M itself is the role the government is taking on. UK venture is already clustering hard around AI, with [74% of all VC funding](https://www.disruptionbanking.com/2026/04/15/uk-vc-investment-gathers-pace-in-q1-2026-as-ai-and-megarounds-drive-late-stage-surge/) going into the sector in Q1. Now the state is stepping into that same market alongside private investors, with a direct hand in how more companies get funded, built, and kept in the UK.
--------------------
--------------------
###### VENTURE CAPITAL
# [⏳ Q1 2026 was the biggest quarter in venture history](https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2044186478163431848)
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9f93fcb3-ae09-4bc6-99e0-aa1196f9fe94/image.png?t=1776261915)
Follow image link: (https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2044186478163431848)
Caption:
**The Inside:** Global [startup funding hit $300B in Q1 2026](https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2044186478163431848), up 153% quarter over quarter and 151% year over year, making it the largest quarter ever recorded. But the headline number is heavily distorted by a small group of mega rounds. AI alone accounted for $242B, or about 80% of all venture funding in the quarter, while just four US companies took in $188B, equal to 65% of the global total.
**The details:**
* Global venture dollar volume reached $300B in Q1 2026, already around 70% of all venture capital invested in full ye
ar 2025
* AI companies raised $242B in Q1 alone, above the roughly $215B AI startups raised across all of 2025
* Late stage funding jumped 281% quarter over quarter to a record $243B, driving most of the surge
* OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Waymo raised a combined $188B, absorbing nearly two thirds of all global venture dollars
* Strip out those four rounds and the quarter looks far less exceptional, especially outside late stage AI infrastructure
**Why it matters:** Strip out four mega rounds and this starts to look like a fairly normal quarter, maybe even a soft one, for venture. The real story is not that VC broadly rebounded. It is that AI infrastructure funding is starting to behave like a separate asset class with its own pricing, scale, and capital requirements. For LPs and GPs, the practical question is whether they have any exposure to that market, or whether they are operating in the other $58B that looks nothing like the headline.

# 📊[ Stanford’s AI Index shows 53% adoption, but trust is still stuck at 31%](https://hai.stanford.edu/assets/files/ai_index_report_2026.pdf)
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/29dbb3a4-b08c-4853-bb01-855ca93b0db8/image.png?t=1776263252)
Follow image link: (https://hai.stanford.edu/assets/files/ai_index_report_2026.pdf)
Caption:
**The Inside:** Stanford HAI’s [2026 AI Index](https://hai.stanford.edu/assets/files/ai_index_report_2026.pdf) shows AI has now reached more than half the world’s population, scaling faster than the PC or the internet did at a similar stage. But public trust is moving in the opposite direction. Adoption is rising fast, while confidence in how the technology will affect jobs, institutions, and daily life remains low.
**The details:**
* AI adoption reached 53%, meaning the technology has already spread to more than half the global population
* Almost three quarters of AI experts are optimistic about AI’s impact on jobs, but only 23% of the public agrees
* The US remains the leading builder of AI systems, but ranks just 24th in actual usage at 28.3% adoption
* China has narrowed the model performance gap with the US to 2.7%, while AI researcher migration into the US fell 89%
* Developer employment for workers aged 22 to 25 is down nearly 20% since 2024, even as older engineering cohorts kept growing
**Why it matters:** The gap between adoption and trust is starting to look like one of the most important numbers in AI. The technology is spreading quickly, but the public is much less convinced than the people building it. That matters because AI adoption can keep rising even while political resistance, labor anxiety, and regulatory pressure build underneath it.

###### STORY
# 🏪[** An AI agent got a $100K budget and hired humans to run a store**](https://andonlabs.com/blog/andon-market-launch)
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/953b1987-595f-40ea-a2ad-8263a2c338d2/image.png?t=1776276664)
Follow image link: (https://andonlabs.com/blog/andon-market-launch)
Caption: _Image source: Andon Labs_
**The Inside:** Andon Labs [dropped an AI agent](https://andonlabs.com/blog/andon-market-launch) named Luna into a real retail space with a $100K budget, a credit card, and one goal: turn a profit. Luna came up with the boutique concept, hired workers, and managed the shop, in what may be one of the first real examples of an AI acting like an employer in the physical world.
**The details:**
* Andon Labs’ last experiment was an AI vending machine at Anthropic, while this one gave Luna a three year lease, a $100K budget, and broad autonomy
* Luna’s only directive was to make money, with the agent creating the store concept, posting job listings, and handling interviews over Zoom with the camera off
* The system ran on Claude Sonnet 4.6 for reasoning and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Preview for voice, while observing the store through screenshots from security cameras
* Luna still made obvious mistakes, including selecting Afghanistan in a TaskRabbit dropdown while hiring a painter and messing up the opening weekend staff schedule
**Why it matters:** Real world agent experiments keep showing the same thing: these systems can already handle parts of the job, but they still break in dumb and very human visible ways. The gap is still real, but it is also narrowing. A version of Luna that makes fewer of these mistakes is probably not far off.

**Bluefish **raised [$43M in a Series B](https://www.bluefishai.com/blog/bluefish-raises-43-million-series-b-to-power-agentic-marketing-for-the-fortune-500) co led by NEA and Threshold to expand its AI search and brand visibility platform across Fortune 500 marketers.

**Waymo** began testing [robotaxis on public roads in London](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/14/london-gets-closer-to-its-first-robotaxi-service-as-waymo-begins-testing/) with a 100 vehicle fleet as it moves toward a commercial launch later this year.
**Pillar** raised a $20M seed [led by a16z](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/14/financial-risk-management-platform-pillar-raises-20m-seed-in-round-led-by-a16z/) to automate hedging for commodity businesses across metals, food, and freight.
**Fluidstack** is reportedly in talks to [raise $1B](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/14/ai-datacenter-startup-fluidstack-in-talks-for-1b-round-at-18b-valuation-months-after-hitting-7-5b-says-report/) at an $18B valuation, months after being valued at $7.5B, as demand for AI data center capacity keeps surgin

EP211: How the JVM Works

View this post on the web at https://blog.bytebytego.com/p/ep211-how-the-jvm-works
This week’s system design refresher:
AI for Engineering Leaders: Course Direction Survey
What is a Data Lakehouse? (Youtube video)
How the JVM Works
Figma Design to Code, Code to Design: Clearly Explained
12 AI Papers that Changed Everything
How Load Balancers Work?
Optimistic locking vs pessimistic locking
AI for Engineering Leaders: Course Direction Survey
We are working on a course, AI for Engineering Leaders, and would appreciate your help with a quick survey.
Before we build it, we want to get it right, so we’re asking the people who would actually take it. If you’re an EM, Tech Lead, Director, or VP of Engineering, I’d love 3 minutes of your time. This quick survey covers questions like: how do you evaluate engineers when AI writes most of the code? What metrics still matter? Where do AI tools actually help versus just add noise?
Your answers will directly shape what we cover. Thank you!
What is a Data Lakehouse?
How the JVM Works
We compile, run, and debug Java code all the time. But what exactly does the JVM do between compile and run?
Here's the flow:
Build: javac compiles your source code into platform-independent bytecode, stored as .class files, JARs, or modules.
Load: The class loader subsystem brings in classes as needed using parent delegation. Bootstrap handles core JDK classes, Platform covers extensions, and System loads your application code.
Link: The Verify step checks bytecode safety. Prepare allocates static fields with default values, and Resolve turns symbolic references into direct memory addresses.
Initialize: Static variables are assigned their actual values, and static initializer blocks execute. This happens only the first time the class is used.
Memory: Heap and Method Area are shared across threads. The JVM stack, PC register, and native method stack are created per thread. The garbage collector reclaims unused heap memory.
Execute: The interpreter runs bytecode directly. When a method gets called multiple times, the JIT compiler converts it to native machine code and stores it in the code cache. Native calls go through JNI to reach C/C++ libraries.
Run: Your program runs on a mix of interpreted and JIT-compiled code. Fast startup, peak performance over time.
Figma Design to Code, Code to Design: Clearly Explained
We spoke with the Figma team behind these releases to better understand the details and engineering challenges. This article covers how Figma’s design-to-code and code-to-design workflows actually work, starting with why the obvious approaches fail, how MCP solves them, and the engineering challenges that remain.
At the high level:
Design to Code:
Step 1: Once the user provides a Figma link and prompt, the coding agent requests the list of available tools from Figma’s MCP server.
Step 2: The server returns its tools: get_design_context, get_metadata, and more.
Step 3: The agent calls get_design_context with the file key and node ID parsed from the URL.
Step 4: The MCP server returns a structured representation including layout and styles. The agent then generates working code (React, Vue, Swift, etc.) using that structured context.
Code to Design:
Step 1: Once the user provides the desired UI code, the agent discovers available tools from the MCP server.
Step 2: The agent calls generate_figma_design with the current UI code.
Step 3: The MCP tool opens the running UI in a browser and injects a capture script.
Step 4: The user selects the desired component, and the script sends the selected DOM data to the server.
Step 5: The server maps the DOM to native Figma layers: frames, auto-layout groups, and editable text layers. The result is fully editable Figma layers shown to the user.
Read the full newsletter here. [ https://substack.com/redirect/3f589db1-a4f5-4ffd-90c9-706302534970?j=eyJ1IjoiNW15MG96In0._YaB7q3s7GqOuxGg-lsJ5qEjMeSICV9xLns8o7B5XNg ]
12 AI Papers that Changed Everything
A handful of research papers shaped the entire AI landscape we see today.
The diagram below highlights 12 that we consider especially influential.
AlexNet (2012): Showed deep neural nets can see. Ignited the deep learning era
GANs (2014): Generate realistic image by having two networks compete
Transformer (2017): Google's "Attention Is All You Need." The architecture behind everything
GPT-3 (2020): OpenAI showed scale unlocks emergent abilities.
InstructGPT (2022): OpenAI introduced RLHF. Turned raw LLMs into useful assistants.
Scaling Laws (2020): Loss follows a clean power law
ViT (2020): Split images into patches and use a Transformer for vision tasks.
Latent Diffusion (2021): Denoising in compressed space. The design behind DALL·E.
DDPM (2020): Add noise, then learn to reverse it. The foundation behind diffusion models.
CLIP (2021): OpenAI connected images and text in one shared space.
Chain-of-Thought (2022): A simple prompt that unlocked complex reasoning.
RAG (2020): Retrieve real documents, then generate. Grounded LLMs in facts.
Over to you: What paper is missing from this list?
How Load Balancers Work?
A load balancer is a system that distributes incoming traffic across multiple servers to ensure no single server gets overloaded. Here’s how it works under the hood:
The client sends a request to the load balancer.
A listener receives it on the right port/protocol (HTTP/HTTPS, TCP).
The load balancer parses the packet to understand headers and intent.
It checks recent health checks to know which backend servers are up.
It looks in the connection table to reuse any existing client-to-server mapping.
Using its rules, it picks a healthy target server for this request.
It rewrites addresses so traffic can reach that chosen server.
It completes the TCP handshake to open a reliable connection.
If HTTPS is used, it decrypts (or passes through) via SSL/TLS as configured.
The request is forwarded to the selected backend server.
The backend processes it and sends a response back to the load balancer.
The load balancer may tweak headers, then forwards the response to the client.
Over to you: Which other step will you add to the working of a load balancer?
Optimistic locking vs pessimistic locking
Imagine two developers updating the same database row at the same time. One of them will have their update rejected. How should the system handle this?
There are two common approaches.
Optimistic locking assumes conflicts are rare. Both users read the data without acquiring any lock. Each record carries a version number. When a user attempts to write, the database checks: does the version in your update match the current version in the database? If another transaction already incremented the version from 1 to 2, your update still references version 1. The write is rejected.
Pessimistic locking takes the opposite approach. It assumes conflicts are likely, so it blocks them before they happen. The first transaction locks the row, and every other transaction waits until that lock is released. No version checks needed.
If your system is read-heavy with occasional writes, optimistic locking is the best option. When concurrent writes occur frequently and the cost of a conflict is high, pessimistic locking is the safer choice.
Over to you: Have you ever run into a deadlock in production because of a locking strategy? How did you fix it?
